title: Kernel eval sweep: flash-attention + paged-KV + continuous-batching
content:
Purpose:
This note captures the results of the kernel/runtime change sweep that landed flash-attention v2, paged-KV (8k page size), and continuous-batching heuristics on the staging inference fleet. Goal was to detect regressions in model onboarding evals (chat, summarization, retrieval-qa) and to surface any quality vs. performance tradeoffs introduced by the new kernels.

Top-level summary:
- Perf: Overall token throughput improved 18–42% depending on sequence length/CPU host. Median generation latency (p50) improved ~12% on medium sequences (512 tokens). p95 latency improved in most cases but worsened for very short requests (<32 tokens) when dynamic batching delayed small requests.
- Quality: Most prompt sets show no statistically significant quality delta. Notable exception: long-context summarization promptset (summ- long-ctx-50) shows a soft regression in ROUGE-L (~-2.6 points) and increased hallucination incidence on 5/50 transcripts.
- Regressions correlated with two conditions: (1) paged-KV boundary behavior for sequences that straddle page edges (observed in summarization prompts that include many repeated system tokens), and (2) continuous-batching when max_wait_ms was set high (40ms) causing cross-request KV reuse patterns to produce stale past-kv interactions for some attention kernels.

Experiment design / reproducibility:
- Baseline runtime: runtime@main (kernel: attn-v1, KV: linear, batching: legacy)
- Test runtime: runtime@feature/flash-paged-contbatch (FlashAttn v2, PagedKV page_size=8192, ContinuousBatching max_batch_tokens=2048, max_wait_ms=40, dynamic_batching=true)
- Model: onboarding/redwood-1.3b-fp16 (same model binary for baseline/test)
- Hardware: p4d-like nodes, single-GPU per request runner, CUDA 12.1, cuBLAS/cuDNN matched
- Prompt sets used (seeded runs):
  - chat-onboard-100: 100 multi-turn chat samples (open-domain), eval metrics: helpfulness_score (0–1), safety-flag rate
  - summ-long-ctx-50: 50 long-document summarization prompts (context lengths 6k–10k tokens), metrics: ROUGE-1/2/L, hallucination_count
  - retr-qa-200: 200 retrieval QA prompts with gold answers, metrics: F1, EM
  - code-assist-120: 120 code generation prompts (average 200 tokens), metrics: compile_rate, exact_match_snip
- Each run repeated 6 seeds; run order randomized; logs aggregated with seed and trace_id

Key quantitative diffs (aggregated means, baseline -> test):
- chat-onboard-100:
  - helpfulness_score: 0.78 -> 0.77 (delta -0.01, p=0.12)
  - safety-flag rate: 2.4% -> 2.4% (no change)
  - latency p50 (ms): 210 -> 185 (improve 11.9%)
  - latency p95 (ms): 620 -> 540 (improve 12.9%)

- summ-long-ctx-50:
  - ROUGE-1: 44.1 -> 41.8 (delta -2.3)
  - ROUGE-2: 20.5 -> 18.7 (delta -1.8)
  - ROUGE-L: 38.9 -> 36.3 (delta -2.6)
  - hallucination_count: 3 -> 8 (raw count across 50 samples)
  - latency p50 (ms): 1120 -> 900 (improve 19.6%)
  - notes: regressions concentrated on docs where repeated policy tokens appear near page boundaries (examples listed below)

- retr-qa-200:
  - F1: 78.2 -> 78.6 (delta +0.4)
  - EM: 61.1 -> 61.0 (no sig change)
  - latency p50 (ms): 340 -> 300 (improve 11.8%)

- code-assist-120:
  - compile_rate: 86% -> 86% (no change)
  - exact_match_snip: 32.4 -> 32.1 (delta -0.3)
  - latency p50 (ms): 410 -> 360 (improve 12.2%)

Qualitative failure analysis (summ-long-ctx):
1) Example A (trace_id: abc-20260102-11): source doc contains repeated header block tokenized as long run of the same system prompt. Paged-KV boundary happened mid-header; when FlashAttn v2 fused attention windows across the page boundary the absolute attention weights for the header tokens decreased, and the model skipped an important context sentence when generating the summary. This produced omission + subtle factual drift.
2) Example B (trace_id: abc-20260103-07): continuous-batching pooled two near-simultaneous summarization requests, and background request ordering created a stale KV re-use scenario where a cached page included tokens from the other request; though we expected strict per-request isolation, a micro-bug in page invalidation (paging table TTL) caused ephemeral leakage of context for ~120ms. Result: hallucinated sentence referencing unrelated doc content.

Root-cause hypothesis and supporting evidence:
- Paged-KV page-alignment: our page-aligned KV writes are correct, but read-time offsets for tokens at page edges rely on a rounding heuristic that interacts poorly with FlashAttn's block fusion optimization. When fusion combines two adjacent blocks spanning a page boundary, the effective attention receptive field shifts by a small token offset (1–3 tokens) in some implementations; for dense summarization prompts this moves anchor sentences out of peak attention. Reproduced in unit test with deterministic seed (see linked PR).
- Continuous-batching: default max_wait_ms=40 was too high for low-latency workloads; it increased probability of multi-request batches in edge ordering sequences and exposed a TTL/invalidation gap in the paging metadata. Lowering max_wait_ms reduces the relevant window and eliminated the leak in canary runs.

Mitigations tested (short-term):
- Rollback option: deploy fallback to attn-v1 for summarization workloads via routing policy (product tag: summarization-long-ctx) — proven to remove the ROUGE regressions at cost of 15–20% increased latency for that route.
- Config change: lower continuous-batching max_wait_ms from 40 -> 8 for latency-sensitive routes; dynamic_batching keep enabled. This reduced multi-request batch incidence from ~4.6% -> 0.7% and removed most observed hallucination cases in canary.
- Patch: small fix to page read offset rounding in paged-KV (PR linked). Unit tests added to assert identical attention alignment across page boundaries for synthetic repeated-token sequences.

Longer-term actions:
- Add an onboarding eval check: for any kernel change, run a targeted long-context summarization suite (n=200) with an attention-alignment assertion that compares token-level attention mass on anchor sentences. Fail change if attention mass drop > 12% compared to baseline. (JIRA-INF-7901)
- Improve batching heuristics: implement adaptive max_wait_ms that lowers wait when request-size distribution indicates many short requests. Add a sampling trace that records batch composition and KV page ownership for offline diagnosis. (GH issue #4612)
- Expand promptsets: add more duplicated-prefix tests and system-token-run prompts to the standard onboarding suite; these triggered the paged-KV edge cases.

Immediate recommendations (for product/infra owners):
- Hold feature rollout for production until page-read offset fix lands and continuous-batching default max_wait_ms lowered for hosted-grade routes.
- Ship diagnostic canary with flooding of summarization-long-ctx requests and monitor hallucination_count and attention-mass metric.
- Re-run the full onboarding suite (chat, retr-qa, code, long-summ) after fixes and produce a block-diff report for decision meeting.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Is the attention shift purely an implementation artifact of FlashAttn v2 fusion, or also affected by kernel numeric precision differences on edge tokens? (investigate by running fusion flag off)
- Should we implement a per-route page_size tuning knob for Paged-KV? Some routes benefit from smaller pages when document structures have many repeated small blocks.
- Do we need per-request KV isolation telemetry at the trace level (adds overhead) vs. the rolling TTL approach?

Appendix: short reproduction recipe for the failing long-summ example:
- Checkout runtime PR branch and run example script: tools/repro/run_long_summ_repro.sh --seed 111 --page_size 8192 --flash_fusion on
- Input doc saved in /experiments/summ_repro/doc-abc.txt (attached in the ticket)
- Deterministic seed produces the misaligned attention pattern; inspect attention dump: /tmp/trace-abc-attn.json

Linked artifacts and references:
- runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4523 (paged-KV rounding fix committed)
- telemetry dashboard (canary): https://grafana.redwood.local/d/abcd/onboarding-kernel-sweeps
- JIRA: INF-7892 (kernel sweep), INF-7901 (attention-mass gating)

Notes to reviewers:
- Focus first on the long-context summarization failures — they are the only high-confidence quality regression. Other deltas are within noise.
- The perf wins are real and material; we should avoid blanket rollback if targeted mitigations are quick to deploy.
- I can run the next canary with adaptive max_wait_ms knob if infra wants a dataset to watch.

-- Avery
